reason: The earlier review maps 'flecked' to PATO:0000333 spotted, so 'without flecks' means not spotted.
A pseudoaxillary inflorescence looks axillary but arises beside or above the axil (as in Solanaceae). That fits extra-axillary: arising outside the axil of its leaf or bract.

'Multiseptate hairs' are hairs divided by many cross walls, i.e. multicellular hairs. The word names the kind of hair, and 'with/without multiseptate hairs' then reads as presence or absence of that hair.

target: new: chemical constituent present (CHEBI tannin in the bearer)
reason: This is a chemical constituent of bark or leaves, not a shape or structure. It needs a constituent pattern with a CHEBI class, not a PATO or FLOPO value.
Interwoven hairs or branches are entwined with one another, which is what PATO:0001846 tangled says.
'Sub-' means nearly, so this is horizontal PATO:0001855 marked as approximately, like 'suborbicular'.
'Bithecous' means having two thecae, a count with the counted part inside the word. config/flora_counted_parts.tsv needs a 'thecous' row for anther theca.
A tussock grass grows in a dense tuft or clump from the base, which is FLOPO caespitose (synonym tufted).

label: mitrate
definition: A concave 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like a mitre: a symmetrical, conical cap that is entire or equally lobed at its base and not split up one side. NOTE: Sibling and contrast of FLOPO:0991119 cucullate; the usual word for the moss calyptra. The conic part of 'conic-mitrate' is PATO:0002021 conical.
reason: Mitrate vs cucullate is the standard character of the moss calyptra, and neither PATO nor FLOPO has mitrate. Mitrate calyptrae are conic by definition, so the compound word is this one value.

Epilose means a moss leaf without a hair-point. PO's awn (PO:0025349) is limited to glumes, lemmas and paleas, and there is no moss hair-point class to state as absent. Raise it together with 'piliferous'.

label: succubous
definition: An imbricate quality inhering in the leaves of a leafy liverwort by virtue of each leaf's being obliquely inserted so that its upper (acroscopic) margin lies beneath the lower margin of the next leaf above, like the shingles of a roof. NOTE: Opposite of incubous; botany-specific.
reason: A standard liverwort character with no term. It is a specific kind of overlapping arrangement, so it belongs under FLOPO imbricate.
French 'sans calicule' means without an epicalyx (calyculus). PO:0009063 epicalyx lists calyculus as a synonym.
A pseudo-fascicle is a fascicle-like cluster of inflorescences on a condensed short shoot. It still meets fascicled: borne in a close cluster from about the same point.

label: quincuncial
definition: An imbricate quality inhering in a whorl of five perianth members by virtue of their overlapping in bud so that two members are wholly outside, two wholly inside, and the fifth has one margin outside and one inside. NOTE: An aestivation type, sibling of FLOPO:0991083 valvate.
reason: A standard aestivation type (the way perianth parts overlap in bud) of calyx and corolla, with no term. It is a kind of imbricate.
This is 'slightly keeled': carinate is already ruled to PATO:0002522 keel-shaped, and 'sub-' marks it as approximate.
French 'nervures anastomosées' means veins that rejoin one another: FLOPO anastomosing.
This negates 'locellate' (anther locules divided into locelli), which has no term, and it only states the usual condition. Decide on locellate itself first.
'Unijugous' means one pair of leaflets. That is the existing 'jugate' count (pairs of leaflet) with the number given by the prefix 'uni-'.

target: new: indumentum with hair orientation (pubescent hair PATO_0001320 of the bearer + appressed FLOPO:0991064 of its trichomes)
reason: These are two values with different bearers: the organ is pubescent and its hairs are appressed. It is not one quality, and strigose/strigulose specify stiff hairs.
A bur-like fruit or bract is one beset with spines or hooked prickles, and PATO:0001365 spiny keeps that content. The hooked part is lost.
Non-stipitate means not borne on a stalk, the negation of FLOPO stipitate.

label: self-fertile
definition: A fertile quality inhering in a plant or flower by virtue of its being capable of setting viable seed after pollination with its own pollen. NOTE: Breeding-system quality; PATO:0000344 compatible is relational and not specific to self-pollination.
reason: A breeding-system trait recorded in floras and trait data, with no PATO or FLOPO term. It fits under PATO fertile, as cleistogamous and polygamous were added before.
Toroid means doughnut-shaped, a ring round a central space, which matches PATO:0002539 ring shaped (annular). There are only two short examples on the receptacle, so the sense is uncertain.
Venulose means marked with fine veins, the same rule as 'veined' (C211) on stipules and fruits alike.
For a leaf outline, broadest at the middle is elliptic, in contrast to ovate (broadest below) and obovate (broadest above). Unlike the rejected bare 'broadest', the place is stated.
Homophyllous means all leaves are of one form: the set of leaves does not vary (PATO:0000438 invariant on the leaves). Negating FLOPO dimorphic would miss leaves with three or more forms.
A count with the part in the word (bracteate -> bract is in flora_counted_parts.tsv). The number is 'many', which the count pattern holds as not numeric, like 'few-flowered'.
Negation of FLOPO petaloid.
Not a term of the standard leaf-architecture system. It may mean semicraspedodromous or eucamptodromous, but either way it is a pinnate venation type, so the broader FLOPO value is safe.
PATO:0104365 plicate has the synonym pleated, so 'without pleats' means not plicate.
